results.claim: Between 0.28.0 and 0.44.0, the pi-web-access changelog contains no Breaking or Removed sections and no entry that removes or renames web_search, fetch_content, source_check, or get_search_content.
results.reason: Fetched https://unpkg.com/pi-web-access@0.44.0/CHANGELOG.md (129,991 chars) and read the entire 0.28.0–0.44.0 range directly (0.44.0→0.25.0 in three passes): version headers run "[0.44.0] - 2026-10-20" through "[0.28.0] - 2026-09-04" as the record states, and the only section types in range are Highlights/Added/Changed/Fixed. A full-file search found exactly one "Breaking" occurrence — the word "breaking" inside a 0.30.0-era Fixed bullet ("Prevent malformed `fetch_content` auth, mode, or proxy parameters from breaking tool-call rendering"), not a section header — and four "### Removed" sections, all in old-version content: the librarian skill removal (issues #136/#23), the deprecated code_search tool removal (#61/#62), the package-lock.json removal adjacent to "[0.10.7] - 2026-05-02", and the result-review workflow removal (header unpinned after two bounded attempts; its neighboring entries reference the pi 0.63+ auth migration, consistent with pre-0.17.0 but not pinned). The 0.30.0 sentence the record quotes — "Removed the unconditional global `fetch` replacement during extension initialization; proxy transport is now installed lazily" — appears verbatim inside a Fixed section. My scan of the Changed/Fixed sections in range found real behavior changes to the four tools that a header-only scan would fold into the record's own caveat, none of which remove or rename them: 0.30.0 makes source_check stop inferring support/contradiction (retrieved passages require manual semantic review) and defaults fresh installs to the silent `none` workflow; 0.31.0 truncates long web_search output (full results remain via get_search_content); 0.37.0 marks failed tool calls isError:true (explicitly covering web_search and source_check); 0.38.0 shortens the web_search tool description; 0.34.0 changes the toolActivation default; 0.28.0 parallelizes batch searches. All four tools remain registered and documented at 0.44.0 (V5).
